source.title: Learning threshold neurons via edge of stability
source.authors: Kwangjun Ahn; Sébastien Bubeck; Sinho Chewi; Y. Lee; Felipe Suarez; Yi Zhang

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes gradient descent dynamics in simplified neural-network models and reports effects of large step sizes and edge-of-stability behavior, conceptually related to V5. It does not test benchmark training classification error.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 experiments report bias and logit dynamics, not training classification error. The paper cites results from prior work, which are not recorded as rows. Its own results on learning threshold neurons and sharpness are recorded where relevant to V5.
record.test_reason: Theorem 2 proves convergence to a global minimizer with limiting sharpness near 2/η in a single-neuron model. This bears on V5's edge-of-stability component through a different method. Threshold-neuron bias and test accuracy alone do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors explain a step-size transition for learning negative-bias threshold neurons through EoS dynamics, prove detailed EoS results for simplified models, and leave an end-to-end analysis of the sparse-coding task open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient descent in a simplified single-neuron model and a mean model for a ReLU network; it does not use the wide-network squared-loss recipe in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The mean-model threshold-neuron outcome changes across the step-size threshold 8π/d²: below it the limiting bias is near zero; above it the bias is negative. The paper also presents CIFAR-10 plots at different initial learning rates, but those figures do not report training error or sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: The mean model's limiting bias stays near zero below 8π/d² and becomes bounded away from zero on the negative side above that threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large gradient-descent step sizes enable negative-bias threshold-neuron learning in the analyzed mean model, whereas smaller steps fail.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 experiments show stronger negative-bias development at larger learning rates; SGD experiments also report lower average activations, indicating sparser representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger learning rates can promote threshold-like neurons and sparse hidden representations in ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 plots are figure-only for the reported dynamics and do not show training classification error or sharpness. The central theorems concern simplified models and rely on specified initialization and nonzero-iterate conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted. Figure 1 reports test accuracy and bias for the motivating sparse-coding setup, not the claim's training classification error; Figures 2, 4, 11 and 13 report dynamics or comparisons that do not directly measure a V5 outcome.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, and dependence on model size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, training speed and trainable depth.

Wide squared-loss networks, the initial linearized-model stability boundary, the full catapult loss-rise-and-recovery sequence, divergence at larger rates or from below the threshold, and progressive sharpening during full-batch training of practical networks. R1 establishes limiting sharpness, not the entire trajectory described by V5.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed limits_scope label based on R2–R3: measuring a different outcome does not qualify V5. Figure 4 directly reports sharpness and EoS behavior in the motivating ReLU model; the record incorrectly dismisses its relevance, but explicitly declares its omission in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing under the supplied rule.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and varying student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, training error, and the effects of shortcuts, normalization-free training, or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for learning speed or trainable depth.

The study does not test wide networks with squared loss, the stability limit of an initial linearized model, or the long-run sharpness behavior described in the claim. It studies simplified models and reports threshold-neuron learning and limiting sharpness.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup-style training without normalization.

rows.subject: single-neuron linear network f(x,y)=ℓ(xy)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in the edge-of-stability regime from the theorem's specified initialization.

conditions.value: xt≠0 for all t≥1 while yt²>2/η

rows.note: The result is a theorem for a simplified single-neuron model, not a wide network or a training-loss result.
rows.check: The sharpness bound is correctly recorded. Include the small-step-size assumptions underlying the asymptotic theorem, including η<1. The theorem also proves convergence to (0,y∞), a global minimizer; it does not establish progressive sharpening.

rows.subject: mean model (A,b)
rows.size_stated: parameterized by dimension d; size otherwise not stated
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with step size η=(8−δ)π/d² from (A0,0).
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes this regime as failing to learn threshold neurons; the measure is bias, not training loss.
rows.check: Limiting bias measures threshold-neuron learning, not V5's loss and sharpness dynamics. The bound is mistranscribed: Theorem 3 gives b∞ ≥ −(η/γ)|A0| = −O_A0,δ(1/d²), without squaring η/γ or |A0|. Bias learning is absent in this regime, but that is not absence of V5.

rows.subject: mean model (A,b)
rows.size_stated: parameterized by dimension d; size otherwise not stated
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with step size η=(8+δ)π/d² from (A0,0).
rows.note: The authors characterize this as successful threshold-neuron learning; no training classification error is reported.
rows.check: The negative-bias bound establishes threshold-neuron learning. This row does not measure loss recovery or sharpness tracking near the stability threshold.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on a binarized CIFAR-10 dataset using the first two classes; cosine learning-rate schedule, with the plotted learning rates as initial values.

conditions.value: full-batch GD, no momentum or weight decay
median bias at last convolutional layer before pooling; plotted against learning rates

rows.measure: Median bias and test accuracy across training dynamics
rows.locator: Figure 3 (bottom), Section 1; details in Section B.2
rows.note: These plots do not report training classification error, loss recovery, or sharpness values; the figure alone does not establish the V5 outcome.
rows.check: Median bias and test accuracy do not establish V1's training classification error or V5's loss and sharpness behavior. The two measures should be separate rows if retained.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Stochastic gradient descent on all ten CIFAR-10 classes; results are shown for batch sizes 100 and 1000.

conditions.value: median bias at last convolutional layer; average activation at last convolutional layer

rows.measure: Median bias and average activation across training dynamics
rows.note: The authors describe qualitatively similar threshold-neuron behavior with larger step sizes, but these measures do not test V5's training-loss and sharpness outcomes.
rows.check: Bias and activation sparsity do not measure any claim version. Separate the two measures and batch-size conditions if these findings are retained.

relationships.condition: Single-neuron linear model with losses satisfying A1–A2, specified initialization in the EoS regime, and nonzero iterates above the threshold
relationships.reason: R1 proves convergence to a global minimizer with limiting sharpness between 2/η−O(η^(1/(β−1))) and 2/η, supporting V5's threshold-sharpness component in this toy setting.
relationships.display_finding: The model converges to a global minimizer with limiting sharpness between 2/η−O(η^(1/(β−1))) and 2/η.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The specified single-neuron model and initialization in Theorem 2
reader_labels.reason: The theorem reports limiting sharpness at or just below 2/η in the EoS regime (R1). This supports the sharpness-threshold aspect in the tested toy setting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The mean model's tested step-size regimes
reader_labels.reason: The study's reported outcome is threshold-neuron bias: it remains near zero below the threshold and becomes negative above it; it does not establish the claim's training-loss recovery in wide squared-loss networks (R2, R3).
